name: Vector Minimalism
summary: Vector Minimalism is a design aesthetic from the early 2010s that is characterized by flat, balanced, geometric shapes, clean, sterile mathematical lines, and a lack of complex textures or gradients.
description: Vector Minimalism is a design aesthetic from the early 2010s that is characterized by flat, balanced, geometric shapes, clean, sterile mathematical lines, and a lack of complex textures or gradients. It succeeded through its absolute dominance in widespread UI/UX design around mid-2013 as a stripped-back direct reaction through the 2000s, 3D, glossy "skeuomorphism" of the Frutiger Aero era movement, along with its hyper-clean, sleek, classic approach that sticks through fast digital rendering, functionality, oversimplicity clear visual hierarchy and technological accessibility against the cluttered design movement from the 2000s.
culturalContext: Vector Minimalism dates back to 2012 where Windows introduced Windows 8/9 with "Flat Metro" elements.

visualDNA.Overview: A lifestyle-oriented, organic, offshoot absolutely gained prevalence in wall art, interior decor and modern print, which changes rigid, maximalist vector paths into hand-drawn, fluid digital shapes, along with color palettes that feature terracotta, beige, soft earth tones, warm sand and muted sage. Another components incorporate abstract continuous, geometrical line art, overlapping semi-circles, simple botanicals, and faces focusing heavily on generous negative space, perfectly symmetrical geometric shapes, and strict grid systems, along with colors that feature deep charcoal grays, vivid, single accent, muted tones to maintain layouts warm yet professional, and entrained palettes…
